mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-1.5% median) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-1% median) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and acceleration of inflation, which increases real discount rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: simultaneous monetary tightening and inflation acceleration
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-1.2% median) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% each for two consecutive months signals a broad-based collapse in residential demand, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall > -1% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate profitability, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (>0.8% median) in at least 65% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months, combined with a simultaneous decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1), indicates a shift from spending to saving, which reduces near-term demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-mo MA for 4 consecutive months AND GDPC1 < 12-mo MA
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-0.9% median) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
